newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks shade back losses at close.
newsitem.headline: French stocks shade back losses at close.

text.p: French shares trimmed their losses at the close on Tuesday in lacklustre holiday trade after sinking earlier on fears of a German interest rate hike to protect the mark.
The shares pared their losses as worriesreceded about the imminence of a monetary tightening by the Bundesbank.
Dealers said they remained cautious but believed the central bank was unlikely to boost rates. "People think the German economy is not yet in a fit state to raise rates," said one trader.
"Worries about German tightening are unfounded," said another trader. "But we could see an upward move in rates in the United States."
Traders said the CAC-40 could come under further modest pressure on Wednesdsay.

The move by the French market to claw back some of its losses in the afternoon "shows there is no sign of panic", said one trader. But another said there were few incentives for the market to move higher in the near term, especially during the month of August when there are fewer players.
"There are not a lot of elements to make it rebound. And now the rise in the dollar is seen as bad news," he said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 8.31 points or 0.28 percent at 2,984.10 while the CAC-40 August futures contract settled eight points lower at 2,989. Volume totalled 7.3 billion francs.

The market started higher on what dealers said was a technical recovery after Monday's nearly two percent loss. But a report by the German research group Ifo suggesting the Bundesbank could intervene to protect the mark and comments by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing to a weekly news magazine that mark stability was a key priority of the central bank pushed it into the red.
Among the losers, Primagaz fell 6.05 percent to 495 francs after forecasting a 30 percent drop in pretax pre-exceptional profit.

Carmaker Renault gained 1.86 percent to 170.0 francs in the aftermath of figures showing its car sales rose 4.1 percent in July, bucking an overall 9.7 percent drop in car sales from 1996 levels which were inflated by a state incentive scheme.
Steelmaker Usinor gained 2.09 percent to 117.50 francs after the announcement of a price rise by its unit Sollac.
